Summary: Core / Platform
Description: Owner: Mhmd Hajeer. Business outcome: preserve the existing Django 6.1 authentication and shared UI foundation while adding exact-group RBAC, settings, numbering, bounded idempotency, practical audit, dashboard integration, and backup readiness. Owning apps/namespaces: apps.accounts/accounts, apps.core/settings, apps.dashboard/dashboard. Boundary: no custom User or Role model, no replacement authentication, and no enterprise audit or idempotency platform.

Summary: Owner/Admin can govern access through the four exact groups
Description: As the pharmacy Owner/Admin, I need deterministic group permissions so every protected action is enforced server-side without changing the existing login flow. Acceptance criteria: Owner / Admin, Pharmacist, Inventory Manager, and Accountant are the only business groups; Owner / Admin receives every model and explicit business permission without requiring is_superuser; anonymous and unauthorized requests are denied; login, session, POST logout, CSRF, navigation behavior, and Django built-in User remain intact. Sources: BRD-SEC-001 through BRD-SEC-005; ERD 4.1-4.2.

Summary: Backend/model: provision groups and permission rules without a Role model
Description: Implement deterministic group/business-permission provisioning and permission guards in apps.accounts/core; preserve framework User, Group, Permission IDs and existing auth flows; coordinate all shared settings and URL changes. No business models beyond approved ERD scope.

Summary: View/template: preserve auth pages and permission-aware navigation
Description: Keep layouts/auth.html, layouts/dashboard.html, shared components, and config.navigation patterns; expose only authorized links while retaining server-side enforcement; do not redesign outside Mhmd Hajeer's UI ownership.

Summary: Tests: authentication, group, permission, and navigation matrix
Description: Test anonymous denial, each exact group, Owner/Admin full permissions without superuser, POST-only CSRF logout, namespace-aware navigation, and unchanged login behavior.

Summary: Owner/Admin can configure pharmacy, tax, and payment settings
Description: As Owner/Admin, I need controlled pharmacy settings so operational screens and posted documents use approved identity, currency, taxes, payment methods, expiry thresholds, and low-stock defaults. Acceptance criteria: only authorized users can change settings; required cash/card/bank transfer methods can be represented; changes append audit events; secrets are never displayed or stored in business settings; posted snapshots do not change retroactively. Sources: BRD-SET-001 through BRD-SET-003, BRD-FIN-004; ERD PharmacySettings, TaxRate, PaymentMethod.

Summary: Backend/model: settings, tax-rate, and payment-method records
Description: Implement ERD-defined UUID entities, Decimal tax precision, validation, deactivation policy, permissions, and audit hooks in apps.core; keep config.settings separate from business settings.

Summary: View/template: settings forms using shared components
Description: Build Owner/Admin-only Django forms and templates under the settings namespace using existing layouts/tokens; never expose environment variables or credentials.

Summary: Tests: settings authorization, validation, snapshots, and audit
Description: Cover unauthorized access, Decimal/range validation, active/inactive payment methods, required method codes, audit creation, and proof that posted snapshots are independent of later changes.

Summary: [BLOCKED: OQ-03] Posted documents receive unique retry-safe numbers
Description: As staff, I need stable unique document numbers so posted orders, receipts, invoices, payments, returns, refunds, counts, and adjustments remain traceable. Acceptance criteria: numbering occurs under lock inside the posting transaction; a retry reuses the original number; posted numbers are immutable; no gapless promise is made. Blocker: OQ-03 must define prefixes, reset/gap policy, receipt sharing, and legal requirements before implementation. Sources: BRD-DOC-002, BRD-DOC-007; ERD DocumentSequence and Section 12.3.

Summary: Backend/model: document sequence and atomic allocator
Description: After OQ-03 is resolved, implement core_document_sequence and a row-locked allocation service for every ERD sequence type; integrate only through domain posting services.

Summary: View/template: display immutable numbers and numbering failures
Description: Expose allocated numbers on relevant detail/print views and show a safe retry message; do not add a separate numbering UI beyond approved settings needs.

Summary: Tests: uniqueness, locking, rollback, and retry behavior
Description: Test concurrent allocation, rollback, voided-number retention, no duplicate number on same idempotency key, and permission enforcement.

Summary: [CRITICAL / AT RISK; BLOCKED: OQ-12] Sensitive posting is audited and idempotent
Description: As Owner/Admin, I need append-only audit and duplicate-posting protection so sensitive stock and financial actions are traceable and safe to retry. Acceptance criteria: AuditEvent records approved actor/action/object/time/context only; IdempotencyRecord is scoped and checked in the same atomic transaction; retries create no duplicate number, transaction, movement, payment, alert, or audit event; no enterprise ledger/event bus is added. Capacity risk: this cross-cuts every domain workflow. Blocker: OQ-12 retention/retry policy. Sources: BRD-AUD-001 through BRD-AUD-004, BRD-IDM-001 through BRD-IDM-005, BRD-SEC-008 through BRD-SEC-009; ERD AuditEvent and IdempotencyRecord.

Summary: Backend/model: practical audit and bounded idempotency primitives
Description: After OQ-12 is resolved, implement approved core entities and reusable service hooks; keep audit append-only; store no secrets; do not add cryptographic chaining or distributed infrastructure.

Summary: View/template: authorized audit history and duplicate-result feedback
Description: Provide permission-protected audit search/detail and safe already-posted feedback using existing shared UI; no hard-delete or edit controls for audit history.

Summary: Tests: full audit action matrix and idempotent retries
Description: Create shared tests covering every BRD-AUD-002 action and repeated submissions across sale, receipt, invoice, payment, return/refund, supplier return, count, and adjustment services.

Summary: [AT RISK: shared UI workload] Each role sees one useful dashboard and actionable alerts
Description: As an authorized staff member, I need one role-aware dashboard so I can see permitted operational or financial priorities without separate role applications. Acceptance criteria: widgets query authoritative records; low/out-of-stock, expiry, discrepancy, finance, and shift information is permission-filtered; unavailable routes remain safely disabled; no duplicate dashboard/report tables are created. Sources: BRD-RPT-001, BRD-INV-020, BRD-RPT-003, BRD-RPT-006; ERD Section 12.5.

Summary: Backend/query: role-aware dashboard and alert queries
Description: Implement permission-filtered query services over authoritative domain tables; preserve apps.dashboard with no new Phase 1 business table.

Summary: View/template: dashboard widgets and alert states
Description: Build accessible shared widgets within the existing dashboard layout and theme; coordinate namespace availability and avoid duplicated navigation.

Summary: Tests: role visibility, empty states, and query correctness
Description: Test all four groups, unauthorized data isolation, unresolved routes, active/resolved alerts, and absence of duplicated persisted summaries.

Summary: Owner/Admin has a documented and tested PostgreSQL/Neon recovery procedure
Description: As Owner/Admin, I need a realistic backup and restore runbook so the pharmacy can recover without committing credentials or production data. Acceptance criteria: strategy and commands are documented; a restore is tested against safe non-production data; result/evidence is recorded; no secrets or backup artifacts enter Git. Sources: BRD-SET-004, BRD-SET-005 and NFR 6.6.

Summary: Documentation/config: write the Neon/PostgreSQL backup and restore runbook
Description: Document prerequisites, safe credential handling, backup, restore target, verification, and rollback expectations without exposing connection strings.

Summary: Operational review: confirm no application UI or secret storage is introduced
Description: Review configuration and documentation against repository environment patterns; backup/restore remains an operational procedure, not an invented admin screen.

Summary: Test: execute and record a non-production restore drill
Description: Perform a safe restore test, verify representative schema/data integrity, and record date/result without committing the database or credentials.

Summary: Inventory / Purchasing
Description: Owner: Hala. Business outcome: manage medicines and parties, receive stock by batch, preserve one authoritative movement ledger, control counts/adjustments/write-offs, and support lightweight purchasing and supplier returns. Owning apps/namespaces: apps.catalog/medicines, apps.parties/suppliers and customers, apps.inventory/inventory, apps.purchasing/purchases, supplier-return portion of apps.returns/returns. Boundary: no shelf/bin tracking, no duplicate stock arithmetic, and no enterprise purchase approval chain.

Summary: Inventory staff can maintain medicine catalog, units, barcodes, and prices
Description: As Inventory Manager, I need accurate medicine master data so purchasing, stock, barcode lookup, and sales share one catalog. Acceptance criteria: medicines include approved attributes and UUIDs; one base unit has conversion 1; conversions are positive; purchase/sale eligibility is enforced; active barcodes are globally unique; price history and posted snapshots are preserved; used records deactivate instead of hard-delete. Sources: BRD-CAT-001 through BRD-CAT-008; ERD Category, Manufacturer, Medicine, MedicineUnit, MedicineBarcode, MedicinePriceHistory.

Summary: Backend/model: catalog entities, constraints, and permissions
Description: Implement ERD UUID/Decimal/timestamp/deactivation conventions in apps.catalog, including exactly-one-base-unit service validation and unique active barcodes.

Summary: View/template: medicine, unit, barcode, and reference-data workflows
Description: Build namespaced Django forms/views/templates with search, validation feedback, active/inactive controls, and availability-only access for Pharmacist.

Summary: Tests: catalog integrity, authorization, and history
Description: Test base-unit/conversion rules, barcode uniqueness/lookup, Decimal precision, deactivation, price history, permissions, and transaction-snapshot protection.

Summary: Staff can maintain suppliers, customers, walk-in context, and prescribers
Description: As authorized staff, I need shared party records so purchases, sales, statements, and prescriptions reference consistent people and organizations. Acceptance criteria: supplier/customer codes are unique; saved parties support approved contact fields and active state; walk-in sales require no Customer row; prescribers support optional identifier/contact; used parties deactivate rather than hard-delete. Sources: BRD-PTY-001 through BRD-PTY-005; ERD Supplier, Customer, Prescriber.

Summary: Backend/model: party entities and role permissions
Description: Implement UUID party models, unique/conditional constraints, PROTECT relationships, deactivation behavior, and group permissions in apps.parties.

Summary: View/template: supplier, customer, and prescriber management
Description: Build suppliers/customers namespaces and forms with permission-specific create/view/change behavior; keep walk-in selection as null customer rather than a fake row.

Summary: Tests: party validation, walk-in behavior, and protected history
Description: Cover uniqueness, optional fields, permissions, deactivation after use, and proof that walk-in flows do not create customer records.

Summary: [CRITICAL / AT RISK; BLOCKED: OQ-01,OQ-02] All domains use one batch ledger and FEFO service
Description: As pharmacy staff, I need one authoritative inventory service so every receipt, sale, return, count, and adjustment produces traceable batch movements and consistent availability. Acceptance criteria: MedicineBatch stores expiry, acquisition cost, base quantity, and receipt reference; StockOperation groups append-only StockMovement rows; FEFO excludes expired/non-positive batches and allocates earliest expiry then receipt order across batches; actual valid-batch deviations are warned and audited; other apps never mutate quantities directly; no shelf/bin fields exist. Blockers: batch cost-layer policy and pharmacy timezone. Sources: BRD-INV-001 through BRD-INV-015, BRD-INV-021 through BRD-INV-022, BRD-CON-001 through BRD-CON-003; ERD MedicineBatch, StockOperation, StockMovement.

Summary: Backend/model: batch, operation, movement, and FEFO allocation service
Description: After OQ-01/OQ-02 decisions, implement approved entities, typed source FKs, Decimal quantities/costs, append-only policy, row locks, deterministic FEFO, and same-transaction batch projections.

Summary: View/template: inventory availability, expiry, and FEFO-deviation feedback
Description: Build permission-aware batch/availability views and clear expired/near-expiry/FEFO warning states using shared components; no direct quantity-edit form.

Summary: Tests: movement authority, FEFO, expiry, concurrency, and app boundaries
Description: Test multi-batch allocation, deterministic order, expired blocking, deviation metadata, append-only history, locked concurrency, rollback, and rejection of direct/negative normal stock changes.

Summary: Inventory Manager can count, adjust, write off, and monitor stock safely
Description: As Inventory Manager, I need controlled reconciliation tools so system quantities can be corrected without losing history. Acceptance criteria: counts snapshot system/count/variance; posting non-zero variance creates movements; adjustment/write-off requires exact batch, actor, reason, and authorization; expired/damaged/lost types are distinguished; low/out-of-stock, near-expiry, expired, and discrepancy alerts are queryable; posted history is retained. Sources: BRD-INV-016 through BRD-INV-020; ERD StockAdjustment, StockAdjustmentLine, StockCount, StockCountLine, InventoryAlert.

Summary: Backend/model: stock count, adjustment, write-off, and alert services
Description: Implement ERD headers/lines, state transitions, document numbering integration, inventory-service posting, reason/actor requirements, and alert generation/resolution.

Summary: View/template: count sheets, adjustment forms, write-offs, and alerts
Description: Build authorized workflows with variance previews, exact-batch selection, blocking validation, warning states, and retained detail history.

Summary: Tests: reconciliation math, permissions, alerts, retry, and history
Description: Test zero/non-zero variance, write-off types, Decimal quantities, exact batches, negative-stock rejection, active-alert uniqueness, idempotent posting, and no hard deletion.

Summary: Inventory Manager can create lightweight purchase orders
Description: As Inventory Manager, I need purchase orders so requested medicines, costs, discounts, taxes, received quantities, and remaining quantities are tracked before receipt. Acceptance criteria: order/item fields follow ERD; statuses are draft, submitted, partially received, received, closed, cancelled; only valid purchase units are used; submitted history is retained; there is no multi-level approval chain. Sources: BRD-PUR-001 through BRD-PUR-004; ERD PurchaseOrder and PurchaseOrderItem.

Summary: Backend/model: purchase order aggregate and simple transitions
Description: Implement order/item UUID entities, Decimal snapshots/totals, validation, numbering integration, permission checks, and approved status transitions in apps.purchasing.

Summary: View/template: purchase order create, edit, submit, and detail
Description: Build supplier/item forms, remaining-quantity display, transition actions, and protected retained history under purchases namespace.

Summary: Tests: order validation, units, transitions, and deletion policy
Description: Test permissions, positive quantities/costs, unit ownership, draft deletion only, numbering, cancellation/closure, and forbidden enterprise approval behavior.

Summary: [BLOCKED: OQ-01,OQ-02] Inventory Manager can partially or fully receive purchase orders
Description: As Inventory Manager, I need goods receipts so received batches increase stock atomically and purchase-order remaining quantities/statuses stay correct. Acceptance criteria: draft receipt has no stock effect; posted lines include order item, unit, quantity, batch, expiry, and actual cost; posting validates remaining quantity and atomically creates/updates batch, operation/movement, received quantity, status, number, idempotency, and audit; concurrent over-receipt is rejected. Blockers: batch cost layers and local expiry date. Sources: BRD-PUR-005 through BRD-PUR-008; ERD PurchaseReceipt and PurchaseReceiptLine.

Summary: Backend/model: receipt aggregate and atomic posting service
Description: After blocking decisions, implement receipt/line entities and a row-locked, idempotent service calling only apps.inventory for positive movements and order-status updates.

Summary: View/template: draft receipt, batch entry, preview, and posted detail
Description: Build partial/full receiving forms with remaining-quantity, expiry, cost, batch, warning, validation, and immutable posted-detail states.

Summary: Tests: partial/full receipt, concurrency, rollback, movement, and retry
Description: Cover draft no-effect, partial/full statuses, over-receipt, invalid/expired data, unit conversion, batch/movement creation, transaction rollback, and duplicate submission.

Summary: [AT RISK; BLOCKED: OQ-03,OQ-04,OQ-07,OQ-13] Supplier invoices preserve totals and balances
Description: As purchasing and accounting staff, we need posted supplier invoices so costs, tax, discounts, receipt references, payment state, and history are accurate. Acceptance criteria: approved snapshots/totals/statuses are stored; posted invoices are immutable except derived payment projections and traceable void/reversal; print data is complete; draft deletion rules are honored. Capacity risk: depends on receipts, finance, numbering, and unresolved invoice/tax/currency policy. Sources: BRD-PUR-009 through BRD-PUR-011, BRD-DOC-004; ERD PurchaseInvoice and PurchaseInvoiceLine.

Summary: Backend/model: purchase invoice aggregate, calculations, and posting
Description: After OQ decisions, implement invoice/line entities, Decimal calculations, snapshots, receipt-link validation, payment projections, atomic/idempotent posting, and history-preserving states.

Summary: View/template: supplier invoice draft, posting, detail, and print data
Description: Build permission-aware forms/detail views with supplier/receipt information, totals, state, balance, and print-friendly content using shared document patterns.

Summary: Tests: invoice precision, snapshots, status, links, and retry
Description: Test Decimal rounding policy once approved, receipt consolidation, due date, posted immutability, balance projection, numbering, rollback, idempotency, and permissions.

Summary: [AT RISK; BLOCKED: OQ-09,OQ-10,OQ-13] Inventory Manager can return exact batches to suppliers
Description: As Inventory Manager, I need supplier returns so unsent stock is removed from the exact batch and the supplier credit remains traceable. Acceptance criteria: return references supplier and purchase when applicable; lines identify medicine, exact batch, quantity, reason, and value; posting atomically creates negative movements and a statement credit; retries do not duplicate effects; posted/void history is retained. Blockers: return credit allocation, currency, and reversal policy. Sources: BRD-PUR-012, BRD-RET-007 through BRD-RET-009; ERD SupplierReturn and SupplierReturnLine.

Summary: Backend/model: supplier return and exact-batch posting service
Description: After OQ decisions, implement return/line entities, value snapshots, stock-operation link, atomic inventory decrease, statement credit projection, numbering, idempotency, and audit.

Summary: View/template: supplier return create, validation, and retained detail
Description: Build exact-batch selection, available-quantity display, reason/value inputs, posting confirmation, credit visibility, and immutable history under returns namespace.

Summary: Tests: batch quantity, credit, permissions, rollback, and duplicate posting
Description: Test supplier/invoice consistency, quantity cap, movement linkage, balance/statement treatment once approved, void/reversal path, and retry safety.

Summary: POS / Sales / Prescriptions
Description: Owner: Malik. Business outcome: deliver pharmacist-facing barcode POS, held sales, prescription records/warnings, authoritative FEFO sale completion, controlled discrepancy override, and professional sales documents. Owning apps/namespaces: apps.sales/sales and apps.prescriptions/prescriptions; consumes apps.catalog, apps.parties, apps.inventory, apps.finance, and apps.core services. Boundary: no clinical advice, no independent stock arithmetic, no expired sale, and no enterprise discrepancy case system.

Summary: [BLOCKED: OQ-05,OQ-06] Pharmacist can record prescriptions and acknowledge warnings
Description: As Pharmacist, I need lightweight prescription records so prescribed medicines and instructions can be associated with sales without the system making clinical decisions. Acceptance criteria: optional customer/prescriber/date/notes and items are stored; attachment is optional only where safely achievable; prescription-required medicines warn and require acknowledgment but do not block; expired stock remains blocked; no medical advice is generated. Blockers: lifecycle, attachment security, and one-versus-many prescription policy. Sources: BRD-PRE-001 through BRD-PRE-005; ERD Prescription and PrescriptionItem.

Summary: Backend/model: prescription aggregate and safe attachment boundary
Description: After OQ decisions, implement ERD entities, validation, permissions, retention, and secure upload rules in apps.prescriptions; do not add clinical logic.

Summary: View/template: prescription forms, details, attachment, and POS warning
Description: Build authorized, accessible records and non-blocking acknowledgment UI; clearly separate prescription warning from absolute expiry blocking.

Summary: Tests: lifecycle, file safety, authorization, warning, and sale association
Description: Test allowed/denied roles, MIME/size/storage decisions, item quantities, retention, acknowledgment, expired-batch independence, and chosen prescription cardinality.

Summary: [BLOCKED: OQ-04,OQ-05] Pharmacist can build a server-validated barcode sale
Description: As Pharmacist, I need a fast POS cart so I can scan or search medicines, choose units/quantities/customer/prescription, see stock/expiry warnings, and preview permitted discount, tax, and totals. Acceptance criteria: known barcode resolves one medicine/unit; unknown barcode creates nothing; manual search remains; keyboard/HID Enter works; server is authoritative for price, discount, tax, stock, and permissions. Blockers: pricing/tax and prescription policy. Sources: BRD-SAL-001 through BRD-SAL-003 and BRD-SAL-005; ERD SalesInvoice draft aggregate and SalesInvoiceLine.

Summary: Backend/model: draft sale/cart validation and barcode lookup
Description: Implement draft SalesInvoice/Line behavior, lookup/query services, unit conversion, stock preview, customer/walk-in/prescription links, and authoritative Decimal preview calculations.

Summary: View/template: keyboard-first POS cart and warnings
Description: Build accessible server-rendered POS with minimal vanilla JavaScript for HID barcode input, manual search, line editing, customer context, prescription association, warnings, and totals preview.

Summary: Tests: barcode, cart, permissions, validation, and browser distrust
Description: Test known/unknown/duplicate barcode behavior, manual search, units, quantities, walk-in/saved customer, warnings, stale/tampered preview rejection, and keyboard submission.

Summary: Pharmacist can hold and resume a sale without reserving stock
Description: As Pharmacist, I need to suspend and resume a cart so I can serve another customer without changing inventory. Acceptance criteria: draft can become held and resume; held lines/totals remain editable under approved rules; no StockOperation, StockMovement, permanent batch allocation, payment, or invoice number is created until completion; unauthorized users cannot access another user's held work except where explicitly permitted. Sources: BRD-SAL-004; ERD SalesInvoice DRAFT/HELD design.

Summary: Backend/model: held-sale transitions and ownership rules
Description: Implement DRAFT-to-HELD-to-DRAFT transitions, retained aggregate state, permissions, and deletion policy with no inventory/finance effects.

Summary: View/template: hold list, resume action, and status feedback
Description: Add POS hold/resume controls and a permission-filtered held-sale list using existing layout/components and minimal JavaScript.

Summary: Tests: no reservation, ownership, transitions, and resume fidelity
Description: Prove holding creates no movement/payment/number, lines survive resume, invalid transitions fail, and unauthorized access is denied.

Summary: [CRITICAL / AT RISK; BLOCKED: OQ-01,OQ-02,OQ-03,OQ-04,OQ-06,OQ-11,OQ-13] Pharmacist can complete an atomic FEFO sale
Description: As Pharmacist, I need one completion action so a valid sale atomically allocates non-expired batches, records stock/cost snapshots, posts invoice/payment/balance, and returns a printable result. Acceptance criteria: permissions/state/units/quantities/warnings are revalidated; FEFO can span batches; actual valid-batch deviation is audited; expired stock is rejected; prices/tax/discount and snapshots are authoritative; movements, initial payment, balance, number, audit, and idempotency target commit together; retry produces no duplicate. Capacity risk: highest-dependency workflow. Sources: BRD-SAL-006 through BRD-SAL-013, BRD-FIN-015 through BRD-FIN-019, BRD-CON-001 through BRD-CON-003; ERD SalesInvoice, SalesInvoiceLine, StockMovement, CustomerPayment.

Summary: Backend/service: atomic sale completion orchestration
Description: After OQ decisions, implement a transaction.atomic and idempotent service that locks sale/batches, recomputes FEFO/totals, calls inventory, creates snapshots/movements/payment/number/audit, and enforces walk-in settlement.

Summary: View/template: completion confirmation, conflicts, and posted result
Description: Build final review, payment inputs, stale-stock conflict handling, FEFO deviation warning/note, blocking expiry errors, and completion/result pages without trusting browser totals.

Summary: Tests: end-to-end posting, FEFO, Decimal, concurrency, rollback, and retry
Description: Cover multi-batch COGS snapshots, taxes/discounts, walk-in/saved-customer balances, prescription acknowledgment, locks, stale previews, rollback, duplicate submission, and immutable completion.

Summary: [AT RISK] Pharmacist can complete a controlled physical-stock discrepancy sale
Description: As Pharmacist, I need a minimal override when non-expired medicine is physically present but recorded stock is short so the sale can complete while reconciliation remains visible. Acceptance criteria: warning shows recorded quantity and audit consequence; explicit acknowledgment and allowed reason are required; other requires note; evidence links sale/line/medicine/observed batch data/actor/time; sale completes atomically without allowing expiry; audit and alerts target Owner/Admin and Inventory Manager; authorized staff resolve through adjustment, count, or no-change; no investigation subsystem is added. Sources: BRD-SAL-014 through BRD-SAL-021; ERD StockDiscrepancy and InventoryAlert.

Summary: Backend/model: discrepancy, alerts, and lightweight resolution
Description: Implement ERD evidence/status entities and completion/resolution services integrated with sale and inventory operations; preserve unresolved acquisition cost for reporting; no case-management fields.

Summary: View/template: explicit override warning, evidence, alerts, and resolution
Description: Build blocking acknowledgment/reason UI, observed batch/expiry fields, role-targeted alert views, and authorized resolution forms with clear expired-stock prohibition.

Summary: Tests: trigger boundary, expiry block, audit/alerts, and reconciliation
Description: Test shortage-only availability, required acknowledgment/note, expired rejection, sale linkage, two group alerts, unknown-cost flag, each resolution type, permissions, and idempotent retry.

Summary: [AT RISK; BLOCKED: OQ-03,OQ-04,OQ-09,OQ-13] Staff can print historically accurate sales invoices and receipts
Description: As staff and customer, we need a clear sales invoice/receipt so items, pharmacy/customer context, pharmacist, discounts, taxes, payments, balance, status, and return/refund references are understandable and stable. Acceptance criteria: output uses stored snapshots, has complete approved fields, is professional/accessible/print-friendly HTML, and offers PDF where reasonably achievable; style is under Mhmd Hajeer's UI ownership. Sources: BRD-DOC-001, BRD-DOC-003, BRD-DOC-005 through BRD-DOC-008; ERD SalesInvoice/Line and payment chain.

Summary: Backend/query: immutable sales document context and PDF decision
Description: Build a permission-safe document query using snapshots, payments, balance, and return/refund references; use the approved numbering/rounding/currency/reversal rules; add PDF only if achievable without unsafe scope expansion.

Summary: View/template: professional print-friendly invoice and receipt
Description: Implement the sales document in feature templates using shared layouts/components and Mhmd Hajeer's visual review; include every BRD-DOC-003 field and accessible print behavior.

Summary: Tests: document completeness, historical snapshots, permissions, and print/PDF
Description: Test required fields, walk-in/saved customer, multiple payments, partial balance, later settings/catalog changes, void/return references, authorization, and PDF path if implemented.

Summary: Finance / Reporting
Description: Owner: Yasser. Business outcome: maintain separate customer/supplier payments and balances, reconcile pharmacist shifts, process customer returns/refunds, provide invoice/statement views, and deliver authorized reports/exports. Owning apps/namespaces: apps.finance/payments and invoices facade, customer-return/refund portion of apps.returns/returns, apps.reports/reports. Boundary: no duplicate invoice/report transaction models, no mutable balance table, no general ledger, and no enterprise cash-management subsystem.

Summary: [CRITICAL / AT RISK; BLOCKED: OQ-03,OQ-10,OQ-11,OQ-13] Staff can post and reverse customer/supplier payments with accurate balances
Description: As authorized finance staff, I need separate payment records so invoices support unpaid, partial, fully paid, multiple-payment, and reversal histories. Acceptance criteria: customer/supplier payments link the correct invoice/party/method/actor/time/reference; amounts are positive and capped; active payment sums derive invoice paid/balance/status; walk-in completes paid; retries do not duplicate; statements can consume the history; no mutable account-balance table is added. Blockers: numbering, credit/refund allocation, credit policy, and currency. Sources: BRD-FIN-001 through BRD-FIN-009; ERD CustomerPayment, SupplierPayment, Section 12.2.

Summary: Backend/model: payment posting/reversal and invoice projections
Description: After OQ decisions, implement finance payment entities and row-locked atomic/idempotent services that update projections without rewriting/deleting history; enforce reference and permission rules.

Summary: View/template: payment entry, history, reversal, and balance states
Description: Build customer/supplier payment workflows and invoice payment panels with method/reference validation, clear unpaid/partial/paid status, and authorized reversal reason.

Summary: Tests: partial/multiple payments, caps, reversals, locks, and retries
Description: Test customer/supplier consistency, payment methods, walk-in rule, overpayment rejection, balance/status recomputation, concurrent posts, rollback, permissions, and duplicate submission.

Summary: Pharmacist can open and close one reconciled cashier shift
Description: As Pharmacist acting as cashier, I need lightweight shifts so opening cash and expected-versus-actual closing cash are retained and discrepancies are visible. Acceptance criteria: one open shift per user; close records time, expected cash, actual cash, discrepancy, and note; expected cash includes cash receipts and refunds; history is retained; there is no separate Cashier group or enterprise cash subsystem. Sources: BRD-FIN-010 through BRD-FIN-014; ERD CashierShift.

Summary: Backend/model: cashier shift and expected-cash calculation
Description: Implement ERD entity, conditional open-shift uniqueness, open/close permissions, Decimal cash calculation over active cash payments/refunds, and audit linkage.

Summary: View/template: shift open, live summary, close, and history
Description: Build pharmacist-owned shift workflow with opening cash, expected cash explanation, actual cash, discrepancy, note, and permission-filtered history.

Summary: Tests: one-open constraint, cash calculation, close, and history
Description: Test concurrent opens, non-cash exclusion, reversed payments, cash refunds, discrepancy formula, required close fields, permissions, and immutable closed history.

Summary: [AT RISK; BLOCKED: OQ-08,OQ-09,OQ-10,OQ-13] Staff can return customer items and issue safe traceable refunds
Description: As authorized staff, I need customer returns/refunds linked to the original sale so quantity limits, safety, batch restocking, refund value, and financial history remain correct. Acceptance criteria: cumulative returns cannot exceed sold quantity; safe approved items restore original batches through inventory; expired/damaged/unsafe items never become sellable; refunds link return/invoice/method/shift and stay within eligible value; posting is atomic/idempotent; original sale remains unchanged. Blockers: restock authority, reversal states, credit/balance treatment, and currency. Sources: BRD-RET-001 through BRD-RET-006; ERD CustomerReturn, CustomerReturnLine, CustomerRefund.

Summary: Backend/model: customer return/refund orchestration
Description: After OQ decisions, implement approved entities and atomic/idempotent service validating cumulative quantities/value, calling inventory for safe original-batch restock, posting refund/shift effects, numbering, and audit.

Summary: View/template: original-sale return selection, safety, refund, and history
Description: Build permission-aware return/refund workflow showing sold/previously returned quantities, original allocations, condition, approval, eligible value, method, and retained posted detail.

Summary: Tests: quantity/refund caps, restocking, unsafe items, rollback, and retry
Description: Test multi-batch restoration, non-resellable exclusion, restock authority, payment/shift effects, credit policy once approved, concurrency, reversal, permissions, and duplicate submission.

Summary: [AT RISK; BLOCKED: OQ-10] Staff can search invoices and view customer/supplier statements
Description: As authorized staff, I need one invoices hub and party statements so sales invoices, purchase invoices, payments, returns/refunds/credits, and current balances are visible without duplicate transaction models. Acceptance criteria: invoices namespace is a read/query facade only; statements derive from authoritative records in time order; role permissions protect financial data; no customer_balance, supplier_balance, or statement table is introduced. Blocker: credit allocation/balance treatment. Sources: BRD-FIN-008, BRD-RPT-003, BRD-RPT-006; ERD Sections 2, 12.2, and 12.5.

Summary: Backend/query: invoice facade and statement services
Description: After OQ-10, implement query services over sales/purchase invoices, active payments, posted returns/refunds/credits, and timestamps; do not persist duplicate invoices or balances.

Summary: View/template: unified invoice search and party statements
Description: Build permission-filtered invoice search/detail links and customer/supplier statement views with totals, statuses, transaction chronology, and empty states.

Summary: Tests: query totals, chronology, permissions, and no duplicate persistence
Description: Test unpaid/partial/paid cases, reversals, returns/credits once approved, date ordering, party isolation, sensitive-role access, and query-only architecture.

Summary: [AT RISK] Authorized roles can view operational and financial reports
Description: As an authorized user, I need role-appropriate reports so sales, purchases, COGS/profit, inventory/valuation, stock alerts, balances/payments, discounts/taxes, best sellers, pharmacist performance, and shift discrepancy can be reviewed. Acceptance criteria: reports derive from authoritative transactions; batch acquisition-cost snapshots drive COGS/valuation; unresolved discrepancy cost is flagged, not zeroed; financial visibility follows permissions; no report transaction tables are created. Sources: BRD-RPT-002 through BRD-RPT-004, BRD-FIN-018 through BRD-FIN-019; ERD Section 12.5.

Summary: Backend/query: approved report catalog over authoritative entities
Description: Implement efficient, permission-scoped query services for every BRD-RPT-002 report; preserve Decimal math and exact acquisition-cost snapshots; flag unresolved cost.

Summary: View/template: report filters, tables, summaries, and warnings
Description: Build role-aware server-rendered report pages using existing components, clear date/filter context, empty states, and unresolved-cost warnings.

Summary: Tests: report reconciliation, role security, and edge cases
Description: Reconcile representative report totals to source transactions; test COGS/valuation, returns/reversals, missing acquisition cost, filters, permissions, and absence of summary-table drift.

Summary: [AT RISK] Important reports and documents can be exported
Description: As an authorized user, I need CSV/XLSX and applicable PDF output so approved reports and documents can be shared or printed. Acceptance criteria: exports use the same authoritative filters/data as on-screen reports; permissions are rechecked server-side; CSV/XLSX cover important reports; PDF is provided only where applicable/reasonably achievable; files expose no unauthorized data. Sources: BRD-RPT-005 through BRD-RPT-006, BRD-DOC-006.

Summary: Backend/service: secure CSV/XLSX and applicable PDF export
Description: Implement export services from existing report/document queries, preserving Decimal/date formatting and authorization; add only necessary approved dependency usage.

Summary: View/template: export actions and printable fallbacks
Description: Add permission-gated export controls, clear format/empty/error states, and print-friendly HTML fallback without creating a separate frontend.

Summary: Tests: export parity, authorization, escaping, and file validity
Description: Compare exports with source queries, test role denial, CSV injection-safe output, workbook validity, Unicode, empty sets, and PDF generation only when implemented.

Summary: [AT RISK; BLOCKED: OQ-09,OQ-10] Posted voids, reversals, and credits preserve history
Description: As Owner/Admin or authorized finance staff, I need traceable corrections so posted invoices, payments, refunds, returns, shifts, and stock effects are never silently edited or deleted. Acceptance criteria: allowed transitions, approval roles, timing, dependent-activity rules, and compensating effects follow an approved state machine; original records remain; projections/statements/audit are updated atomically. Blockers: OQ-09 state transitions and OQ-10 credit treatment. Sources: BRD-PUR-011, BRD-SAL-013, BRD-FIN-006, BRD-SEC-008, BRD-AUD-002; ERD deletion conventions and OQ-09/OQ-10.

Summary: Backend/service: approved void, reversal, and compensating workflows
Description: After OQ-09/OQ-10, implement only approved state transitions with permissions, locks, compensating stock/financial effects, projection recomputation, idempotency, and audit; never hard-delete posted records.

Summary: View/template: correction actions, warnings, reasons, and retained history
Description: Build permission-gated actions that explain downstream effects, require reason/confirmation, show original and compensating records, and prevent disallowed transitions.

Summary: Tests: state-machine permissions, dependencies, compensation, and audit
Description: Test each approved transition, payment/return dependencies, role/time limits, batch and balance restoration, rollback, duplicate requests, immutable originals, and audit coverage.
